Marc Fradera-Soler




He/him



Postdoctoral researcher at Stockholm University (Sweden). Botanist working on plant diversity and evolution, with a strong focus on deserts and succulent floras. Previous work includes evolution of genus Crassula (Crassulaceae) in southern Africa, and macroevolutionary patterns of drought–frost resistance in plant groups occurring in hot and cold deserts worldwide.

Bharti Parihar




She/her



PhD student at the University of Florida (U.S.) whose research integrates plant systematics, genomics, developmental biology, and ecophysiology to understand the evolution of specialized traits in succulent and dryland plants. My work spans scales from gene expression and developmental morphology to genome evolution, phylogenomics, photosynthetic physiology, and macroevolutionary trait reconstruction.

text:
Connect, collaborate and advance dryland flora research
The Dryland Floras Network brings together botanists, ecologists and researchers from across disciplines who are working to understand, document and conserve the diversity and evolution of dryland floras worldwide.
From arid deserts and semi-arid steppes to grasslands, savannas and woodlands, our network connects expertise across regions, disciplines and dryland systems, creating opportunities to share knowledge, build collaborations and develop new research. Through the network, you can:

Connect with researchers worldwide working on dryland floras and discover expertise across regions and disciplines.
Share knowledge and ideas across different dryland systems, helping bring together insights that might otherwise remain geographically or disciplinary isolated.
Find collaborators and new research opportunities through a dynamic directory of researchers, institutions and expertise.
Get involved in collaborative initiatives that support research, outreach, understanding and conservation of dryland floras.

Whether you are looking for collaborators, sharing your expertise, or simply want to connect with others working on dryland floras, the network is a place to start.
